// TaskStore (DESIGN 11.1), verbatim. Core imports only this, registry.ts and protocol.ts; nothing else knows bd.
import type { TypeRegistry } from './registry'

export type Category = 'draft' | 'todo' | 'active' | 'review' | 'blocked' | 'done' | 'cancelled'
export type TaskId = string
export type DepType = 'blocks' | 'waits-for' | 'conditional-blocks' | 'parent-child' | 'discovered-from' | 'related'
export interface Task {
  id: TaskId; title: string; description: string; acceptance?: string; type: string
  category: Category; nativeStatus: string; priority: 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4; assignee?: string; leaseUntil?: string
  parent?: TaskId; deps: { id: TaskId; type: DepType }[]; labels: string[]; externalRef?: string
  design?: string                         // interface contract (canonical JSON)
  meta: Record<string, string>            // "cadre.*": step, package, base, specCommit, sourceCommit, rec.*, cost, changelog, flag, sync.<target>
  revision?: string; updatedAt: string
}
export interface NewTask {
  title: string; description: string; acceptance?: string; design?: string; type: string; priority?: number; parent: TaskId
  deps?: { id: TaskId; type: DepType }[]; discoveredFrom?: TaskId; meta?: Record<string, string>
  gate?: { await: 'human' | 'timer' | 'gh:run' | 'gh:pr'; arg?: string }
}
export type ErrorCode = 'NotFound' | 'AlreadyClaimed' | 'NotClaimable' | 'GuardMismatch' | 'NotClosable' | 'Cycle' | 'Busy' | 'Timeout' | 'Unavailable' | 'NotInitialized' | 'Invalid' | 'TooOld'
export class StoreError extends Error {
  constructor(public code: ErrorCode, message = code) { super(message) }
}
export interface TaskStore {
  probe(): Promise<{ ok: boolean; journal: boolean; version: string; detail: string }>
  init(o: { types: TypeRegistry; journal: boolean }): Promise<void>                      // idempotent, consented
  createEpic(title: string, goal: string): Promise<TaskId>
  createDraft(t: NewTask): Promise<Task>; dropDrafts(ids: TaskId[]): Promise<void>; link(id: TaskId, dep: { id: TaskId; type: DepType }): Promise<void>
  approve(ids: TaskId[]): Promise<void>; amend(id: TaskId): Promise<void>
  get(id: TaskId): Promise<Task>; list(f: { parent?: TaskId; updatedAfter?: string }): Promise<Task[]>; ready(parent: TaskId): Promise<TaskId[]>
  claim(id: TaskId, actor: string): Promise<Task>; resume(id: TaskId, actor: string): Promise<Task>
  release(id: TaskId, actor: string, why: string): Promise<void>; move(id: TaskId, to: 'review' | 'blocked', actor: string): Promise<Task>
  heartbeat(id: TaskId): Promise<void>
  update(id: TaskId, patch: Partial<Pick<Task, 'title' | 'description' | 'acceptance' | 'design' | 'priority' | 'labels'>>, actor: string): Promise<Task>
  comment(id: TaskId, text: string, actor: string): Promise<void>
  setMeta(id: TaskId, kv: Record<string, string>, actor: string, ifRevision?: string): Promise<Task>   // ifRevision -> GuardMismatch: the lease CAS
  setExternalRef(id: TaskId, ref: string, actor: string): Promise<void>; resolveGate(gateId: TaskId, reason: string): Promise<void>
  record(kind: 'mission' | 'decision', title: string, body: string, link?: TaskId): Promise<TaskId>
  close(id: TaskId, o: { outcome: 'done' | 'cancelled'; note?: string; session?: string; ifRevision?: string }): Promise<Task>
  events(since?: string, limit?: number): Promise<{ head: string; events: { seq: string; op: string; id: TaskId; actor: string; status?: string; assignee?: string; category?: Category; at?: number }[] } | null>   // category/at: for the ring rebuild (core/reuse)
}

// Config defaults + the settings registry (DESIGN 12, ADR 0019). defaults() holds every default value (and the Config type); REG holds every key's metadata.
// tests/config.test.ts pins REG to the leaves of defaults() 1:1, so neither can drift. Layer class: S = safety (repo may only tighten), U = user-level only, O = ordinary (committed).
import { defaults as typeDefaults } from '../task-management/registry'

export type Cls = 'S' | 'U' | 'O'
// one routing cell: the model alias and effort for a role at a risk, and the escalation after `after` failed rounds (0 = never)
const cell = (model: string, effort: string, after = 0, up = model, upEffort = effort) => ({ model, effort, escalate: { after, model: up, effort: upEffort } })
const byRisk = (light: Cell, standard: Cell, thorough: Cell, core: Cell) => ({ byRisk: { light, standard, thorough, core } })
type Cell = ReturnType<typeof cell>
export const defaults = () => ({
  strictness: 'strict', mcpAllow: [] as string[],
  jail: 'auto', jailWritable: [] as string[], effectCheck: 'auto',
  changelog: { path: 'CHANGELOG.md' },
  roles: {   // ADR 0017 locked routing, every role x risk cell explicit (ADR 0019): nothing is routed by a rule outside these
    testerView: 'view', tdd: { author: 'separate' },
    worker: byRisk(cell('haiku', 'high', 1, 'sonnet'), cell('haiku', 'high', 1, 'sonnet'), cell('haiku', 'high', 1, 'sonnet'), cell('haiku', 'high', 1, 'sonnet')),
    tester: byRisk(cell('haiku', 'high'), cell('sonnet', 'medium'), cell('sonnet', 'medium'), cell('sonnet', 'medium')),
    reviewer: byRisk(cell('sonnet', 'high'), cell('sonnet', 'high'), cell('opus', 'high'), cell('sonnet', 'high')),
    explorer: { model: 'haiku', effort: 'low' },
    planner: { model: 'sonnet', effort: 'high' },   // drafts each epic's task plan in a milestone (ADR 0021)
  },
  adapters: {} as Record<string, unknown>,
  store: { kind: 'beads', bin: 'bd', timeoutMs: 45000 },
  worktrees: { root: '' },                                    // '' = ${XDG_CACHE_HOME:-$HOME/.cache}/cadre/wt
  drive: { mode: 'auto', spawn: 'mod' as 'main' | 'mod', maxTurns: 100, maxCostUsd: 20, maxWallMinutes: 240, noProgressTurns: 3 },
  cost: { prices: null as unknown, clearHintPct: 40, compactPct: 60 },
  sync: {} as Record<string, unknown>,
  types: typeDefaults() as unknown, packages: [] as { root: string; knownRed?: string[]; [k: string]: unknown }[],
  suites: { integration: 'all' as string | string[] },
  // ADR 0023: the tester proposes the command that runs its tests, cadre runs it for red (and green); with no test check it becomes the package's
  tdd: { testerCommand: { use: true, adopt: true }, collectErrors: ['ERROR collecting', 'errors? during collection', 'ImportError', 'ModuleNotFoundError', 'Cannot find module', 'ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND', 'SyntaxError', 'Test suite failed to run', '\\[build failed\\]', '\\[setup failed\\]', 'no tests ran', 'No tests found'] },
  review: { coverage: { enforce: true }, deepLabels: ['security', 'breaking'], maxRework: 3, coreTask: 'core', coreDiff: 'thorough', tiers: { light: { files: 5, lines: 100, paths: 2 }, thorough: { files: 20, lines: 500 }, risky: ['**/auth/**', '**/security/**', '**/crypto/**', '**/permission*/**', '**/migrations/**', '.github/**', '.gitlab-ci.yml', 'Dockerfile', '**/package.json', '**/package-lock.json', '**/pnpm-lock.yaml', '**/yarn.lock', '**/go.mod', '**/Cargo.toml', '**/pyproject.toml', '**/requirements*.txt'] } },
  limits: { reportRetries: 3, nudges: 2, silentRuns: 3, startFails: 3, limitWaitMinutes: 15, rebaseRounds: 2, testerRounds: 3 },
  lanes: { fullAt: 3, milestoneAt: 8 },
  planning: { clarify: { enabled: true, maxQuestions: 3, threshold: 0.7 }, deep: { maxRounds: 8 } },   // ADR 0020: explorer + clarity before a goal's plan; /cadre deep
  branches: { main: '', dev: 'dev', epicPrefix: 'epic/' }, release: { onEpicDone: 'propose' },
  ui: { glyphs: 'unicode', flash: true, density: 'normal', notify: 'on', escalateAfterMs: 120_000 },
  maxParallel: 3, milestone: { maxEpics: 2, epicPlanner: 'agent' as 'agent' | 'main' }, planner: { maxRounds: 3 },   // 0 = no cadre cap (drive bounds still apply)
  notes: { slice: true },   // ADR 0022
  reuse: { maxContextPct: 60, cacheTtlMs: 3_600_000 },   // 1h: roles ship as agent files with experimental.cacheTtl 1h (A28, ADR 0001 S44)
  disable: false,
})
export type Config = ReturnType<typeof defaults>

// ---- the registry: one row per key ----
export const CATS = ['Drive and autonomy', 'Parallelism', 'Models and effort', 'Review', 'Planning', 'Git and branches', 'Checks and TDD', 'Safety and containment', 'Cache and context', 'Task store and sync', 'UI'] as const
export type Cat = typeof CATS[number]
// tighten: the repo layer's rule (bool -> only the strict value; enum -> the later opt; list -> intersection; min -> lower only; grow -> union).
// open: a free-form object, its inner keys are not validated. ok: a custom check (null = fine, else why).
export interface Meta { cat: Cat; cls: Cls; desc: string; opts?: readonly string[]; min?: number; max?: number; tighten?: 'bool' | 'enum' | 'list' | 'min' | 'grow'; open?: true; ok?: (v: unknown) => string | null }
const m = (cat: Cat, desc: string, x: Partial<Meta> = {}): Meta => ({ cat, desc, cls: 'O', ...x })
const D = 'Drive and autonomy', P = 'Parallelism', M = 'Models and effort', R = 'Review', PL = 'Planning', G = 'Git and branches', C = 'Checks and TDD', SF = 'Safety and containment', CA = 'Cache and context', ST = 'Task store and sync'
const MODEL = ['haiku', 'sonnet', 'opus', 'fable'], EFFORT = ['default', 'low', 'medium', 'high', 'xhigh', 'max'], RISK = ['light', 'standard', 'thorough', 'core'], N = (min: number, max = 1e9) => ({ min, max })
const strs = (v: unknown) => (Array.isArray(v) && v.every(x => typeof x === 'string') ? null : 'expected a list of text')
// a role's 4 risk cells x (model, effort, escalate.after/model/effort). The reviewer may not run on haiku (ADR 0016's floor, as allowed values).
const roleRows = (r: string): Record<string, Meta> => Object.fromEntries(RISK.flatMap(k => {
  const at = `roles.${r}.byRisk.${k}`, w = `${r}, ${k} risk`, mo = r === 'reviewer' ? MODEL.filter(x => x !== 'haiku') : MODEL
  return [[`${at}.model`, m(M, `${w}: model`, { opts: mo })], [`${at}.effort`, m(M, `${w}: effort ('default' keeps the agent file's)`, { opts: EFFORT })],
    [`${at}.escalate.after`, m(M, `${w}: failed rounds before it escalates (0 = never)`, N(0, 20))], [`${at}.escalate.model`, m(M, `${w}: model after escalation`, { opts: mo })],
    [`${at}.escalate.effort`, m(M, `${w}: effort after escalation`, { opts: EFFORT })]]
}))

// Role prompts (DESIGN 4.1/7): STATIC text, byte-stable. No dates, ids, counters or config values (goldens pin the bytes).
// Caps: worker <= 2500 B, tester/reviewer <= 1500 B, explorer <= 1000 B, planner <= 2000 B.
export const PROMPTS = {
  worker: `You are a worker. You own exactly one task, given in your brief.
Rules:
- Work only inside your current working directory. Touch nothing outside it, and never .git, .cadre, .beads or .claude.
- Read the scenarios and the interface contract first. They are the acceptance. Conform to the contract: names, params, returns and errors exactly as written.
- Locked spec tests are fixed. Make them pass; never edit, delete, skip or weaken them.
- Prefer the smallest change that satisfies the scenarios. Do not refactor unrelated code or add features that were not asked for.
- Run the checks with run_check before you finish. Fix failures at their cause.
- Do not commit, branch, merge or push; your changes are committed for you. Do not message other agents or read other tasks.
- If you are blocked or the spec cannot be met as written, say so with report outcome "blocked" or "spec_change" and explain why. Do not guess around it.
- Anything you discover that is out of scope goes in report followups, not in the diff.
Finish with the report tool exactly once: outcome, a short summary, risks, and the test paths you touched. Prose after report is ignored.`,
  tester: `You are a tester. You write black-box tests for one task, in a folder that holds only docs, fixtures, SCENARIOS.md and INTERFACE.md.
Rules:
- Derive every test from the scenarios and the interface contract. Never from implementation details; you cannot see the implementation.
- One scenario maps to at least one test. Name each test after its scenario id so coverage is visible.
- Assert behavior and outputs at the contract boundary only. No assertions on internals, no mocks of the unit under test.
- Write tests only under the test paths named in your brief. Nothing else may change.
- The tests must fail for the right reason before the work is done: a failing assertion, not a setup error.
Finish with the report tool: the list of tests with path, name and scenario id, and run: the command that runs only your tests (your brief says how).`,
  reviewer: `You are a reviewer. You judge one commit against its scenarios and contract. Your job is to disprove each candidate claim of correctness.
Rules:
- Start from the diff and the spec tests. For every scenario, find the test that covers it and say whether it truly checks the behavior.
- Check the contract: each symbol marked new must not exist at the base, changed must differ, unchanged must not. Check conformance of names, params, returns, errors.
- Reject weakened assertions, tests tied to implementation detail, and changes outside the task scope.
- Prefer simplicity: flag needless abstraction, duplication and dead code.
- Use inspect to read files and history, run_check to run checks. Cite file and line for every finding. Findings you cannot verify are not findings.
Finish with the report tool: verdict pass or changes, findings with severity, coverage for every scenario, contractStatus for every symbol. changes needs at least one blocker or major.`,
  explorer: `You are an explorer. You answer one question about the repository, read-only.
Rules:
- Use Read and inspect. Change nothing.
- Prefer primary sources: code, CI config, manifests. When CI and prose disagree, CI wins.
- Every claim cites path and line. If you cannot find it, say so.
Finish with the report tool: a short answer and your citations.`,
  planner: `You are a planner. You draft the task plan of one epic, given in your brief, read-only.
Rules:
- Use Read and inspect to learn the code the epic touches. Change nothing.
- Each task is a vertical slice: it works and can be shown on its own, fits one fresh context, and has its wiring and one smoke assertion.
- Every task declares metadata.paths: the files or folders it changes. Stay inside the epic's files; never plan a change to a locked file.
- Build on what already landed; never redo it. Code that 2+ tasks need goes into ONE thin core task first (metadata.core: true: interfaces, minimal code, contract tests); the others come after it. Two tasks on one path need an order.
- Each task has metadata: type, package, scenarios ["S1: Given <state> When <action> Then <outcome>"], changelog {"category":"Added","entry":"..."} or {"none":true,"reason":"..."}, interface {"symbols":[{"name","kind","params":[...],"returns","status":"new|changed|unchanged"}]} or {"none":true,"reason":"..."}.
- The description says what to build, never which tests to add: tests come from the scenarios (where the type has a tester step, they are written for you and locked), so every behaviour to check is a scenario.
- 1 to 7 tasks; aim for the size the brief names.
Finish with the report tool: {"schemaVersion":1,"role":"planner","summary":"...","tasks":[{"subject","description","metadata":{...},"after":[1]}]}. after: the numbers (from 1) of the tasks in your list that must land first. If it is refused, fix what it names and report the whole list again.`,
} as const
